turns.t: Hi there! I get these terrible headaches every spring, always around the same time, and I've finally decided to ask someone about it.
I'm glad you did. Tell me what they feel like.
Like a hot poker behind my right eye. It's the worst pain I've ever had, honestly.
How long does an attack last?
About an hour, sometimes 90 minutes. Then it goes.
How many times a day?
Two or three, and often at night. It wakes me up.
How long does the run of headaches go on for?
Six weeks or so, then they just stop.
Any watering of the eye, or a blocked nose on that side during the attack?
Yes! The eye waters like a tap, and my nose runs on the right side. How did you know?
That's a very typical pattern. Do you stay still or pace about during an attack? ~
I can't sit still. I pace up and down. ~
That's also typical. Any nausea, or flashing lights before it? ~
No. Nothing like that. ~
Have you had any head injury, or any weakness, or any change in your vision between attacks? ~
None of that, no. I'm perfectly well in between. ~
And is there a family history of migraine or headaches? ~
My uncle had something like it, I think. But I don't really know. ~
This sounds like cluster headache, which comes in runs, often in the same season each year.
Is it serious? Is it a tumour? ~
Cluster headache is painful but not dangerous in itself. Because your story is so typical, I wouldn't expect a scan to show anything. ~
That's a relief. Is there treatment? ~
Yes. There are treatments for stopping an attack, and ones for preventing the run. I'd like to refer you to a neurologist to plan it properly.
That makes sense. ~
I'll write the referral letter today, and the neurology team will contact you directly. ~
Good, thank you. ~
Meanwhile, avoid alcohol during a run, as it can set off an attack.
Yes, that's true, now you say it. ~
If the pain changes, or you get weakness, confusion or a stiff neck, come in at once.
I will. Thank you so much. ~
